consensus_summary: The blind responses agree that 'seed' is a multivalent symbol with two dominant strands: (1) the Word of God/gospel sown into hearts (Luke 8:11; Matt 13; Mark 4; 1 Pet 1:23), and (2) offspring/descendants culminating in Christ as the promised messianic Seed (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16). Secondary recognized strands include children of the kingdom (Matt 13:38), death-and-resurrection (John 12:24; 1 Cor 15), faith/kingdom growth (mustard seed), and sowing-reaping consequences.
book_summary: The book defines seed as 'a generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind,' then explicitly distributes this across the same contexts the consensus lists: in the sower it is God's word; in the wheat and tares it is children (of the kingdom); the promised Seed is Messiah; and one planted person (e.g., Abraham) may grow into a house, people, or nation-tree.
consensus_core_identification: Seed = a context-dependent generative symbol whose chief referents are (a) the Word of God sown into hearts and (b) offspring/descendants culminating in Christ the Messiah, with children of the kingdom, kingdom growth, and death-to-fruit as recognized subsidiary senses.
book_core_identification: Seed = a generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind, instantiated as God's word (sower), children (wheat and tares), Messiah (promised Seed), and a planted person growing into a people or nation.
boundary_disagreement: None of substance. The book unifies the consensus's separate strands under a single abstraction ('generative word or life reproducing after its kind'), and its application of Isa 51:2 (one planted person, Abraham, growing into a nation-tree) is a mildly distinctive emphasis, but it falls within the consensus's offspring/Abrahamic-seed and mustard-seed/kingdom-growth strands rather than admitting or excluding new cases.
material_contradiction: None. Every specific identification the book makes (word of God, children of the kingdom, Messiah) is explicitly present in the consensus responses, including Response C's listing of Matt 13:38 (good seed = sons of the kingdom).
rationale: The book's entry is essentially a compressed restatement of the consensus's multivalent account. Its definition-level abstraction ('generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind') is a framing device, not a rival referent; when cashed out, the book names exactly the same core cases the consensus names: seed as God's word in the sower, seed as children in the wheat and tares, and the promised Seed as Messiah. The added Genesis 1:11-12 'after its kind' framing and the Abraham-as-planted-person image (Isa 51:2, mustard seed becoming a tree) are elaborations consistent with, and largely contained in, the consensus alternatives on offspring and kingdom growth. There is no boundary redrawn, no case reclassified against consensus, and no replaced referent.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book REFINES the consensus by subsuming all senses under a single generative principle ('reproduce after its kind,' Gen 1:11-12) and by adding the person-grown-into-nation reading of Isa 51:2 and Matt 13:31-32, which no blind response states in exactly that form; a strict reader might treat that unification and the nation-tree extension as a material change of precision rather than mere wording.
